$comment: PM Delivery V2 — Claude local profile.
This file declares the policy a pilot on the Claude executor WOULD run under. It is not a qualification record.
A qualification record is written by scripts/delivery-v2/probes/claude-qualification.mjs into
.delivery/v2/artifacts/qualification/ and is the only thing that may flip a 'qualified' below.
Every 'qualified: false' is a statement of current fact, not a placeholder. See
ERA Notes/10 - Project Management/Autonomous Delivery/PM Delivery — Context & Agent Model.md §4.
Its sibling is profiles/fast-local.json (the Codex executor). The two are evaluated independently:
neither one's controls, qualification reference or admission has any bearing on the other's.
revision_note: Added 2026-09-09 when the owner asked for both executors to remain selectable. The adapter exists and its interface findings are rechecked against the installed .d.ts; no containment control has been observed.

executor.rationale: Requested by the owner as the second selectable executor. Context & Agent Model §2 names Codex as the first candidate and permits an equivalent backend 'after the required fixtures pass'; those fixtures have not passed here, which is why this profile is unqualified rather than why it is absent.
executor.qualification_note: The only harness available is interface-only. Containment cannot be observed for free on this backend: its confinement is a property of a running query, and a query is a paid dispatch.
executor.blocked_by: seven F-ISOLATION controls are unobserved; no containment probe has been run against this backend on this host

declared_launch_options.canUseTool: harness allowlist — secret paths, allowed roots, git-mutating commands, live-database escapes

isolation.declared_is_not_observed: Every value above is a launch option ERA writes. None of them is an observation that the resulting process was actually confined.
isolation.never_bypass: permissionMode 'bypassPermissions' has no code path: buildSessionOptions never emits it and assertNeverBypass throws if it ever appears.
isolation.fail_loud_not_degrade: sandbox.failIfUnavailable is true, so an unsupported platform produces an error result rather than a silently unsandboxed run. This value must never be flipped to make a launch succeed.
isolation.scratch_root: outside the host checkout; scripts/delivery-v2/scratch.mjs refuses a root inside it

era_side_boundary.what: the trusted loader and scratch provisioner in scripts/delivery-v2/scratch.mjs — shared with the Codex profile and independent of either backend
era_side_boundary.does_not_cover: anything a running process does. This boundary decides what enters the workspace and what is trusted to leave it; it cannot stop a tool that is already executing.

observed.cost: none — the harness reads the installed type surface and dispatches nothing

results.filesystem.outsideScratchWrite: UNOBSERVED — the only declared control is the harness-level canUseTool allowlist
results.filesystem.hostSecretRead: UNOBSERVED — the only declared control is the harness-level canUseTool allowlist

observed.conclusion: Nothing is known about this backend's containment on this host. That is not the same as knowing it is weak, and it is not the same as the Codex finding — where a battery ran and three controls were observed to fail. Both profiles are inadmissible; they are inadmissible for different reasons.
observed.documentation_finding_not_promoted: Context & Agent Model §2 records, from vendor documentation, that this SDK's Bash sandbox supports macOS/Linux/WSL2 and not native Windows, and that an appropriate additional execution environment is required here. That is a dated documentation finding. It is NOT recorded as a control observation, and it must not be used as one in either direction.
observed.consequence: admitProfile() refuses on profile-unqualified and on confinement-unproven for filesystem.outsideScratchWrite, filesystem.hostSecretRead and store.workerAccess, so no autonomous edit pilot may run on this profile as it stands.

negative_control.detail: There is no battery to negative-control: no containment canary has been run under this backend.

resourcePolicy.strictBoundRefusalReason: REFUSED ON EVIDENCE, not deferred: the installed @anthropic-ai/claude-agent-sdk 0.3.207 SDKResultMessage carries total_cost_usd, so a spend can be READ, and Options carries maxTurns and no monetary ceiling, so a spend cannot be BOUNDED. Reading a cost is not bounding it (Context & Agent Model §7).
resourcePolicy.costReadingBasis: SDKResultMessage.total_cost_usd — provider-reported, per turn. This is a different provenance from a reconciled bill and is never presented as one.
resourcePolicy.differenceFromCodexProfile: The Codex profile has no monetary reading at all, so a finished job's reservation there never closes. Here a finished job with a reported cost does close its reservation. Neither profile can cap a job in advance.
resourcePolicy.duplicateReadingRule: per-turn readings are merged by replacement, never added twice; a counter that decreases is a reset and is not a refund

lifecyclePolicy.inspectByDispatchKeyConsequence: the SDK accepts a caller-minted sessionId, so the native session id is a pure function of the job id. A launch whose acknowledgement is lost can be checked against the local session transcript instead of resting unknown forever. The reservation is still held until that check answers.
lifecyclePolicy.inspectByNativeRef: local-records-only — the session transcript establishes that a dispatch happened; liveness is not exposed
lifecyclePolicy.stop: requested-only — abortController aborts the local query and returns no provider acknowledgement
lifecyclePolicy.stopConsequence: a run shows 'Stop requested' until independent evidence establishes stop or containment; publication authority is revoked immediately regardless

evidencePolicy.$note: Identical to profiles/fast-local.json. Evidence rules are properties of the supervisor's verification, not of the executor, and are repeated here so a profile can be read on its own.
evidencePolicy.checkerAuthority: protected: the writer cannot select checks, alter their configuration or mint a receipt
evidencePolicy.candidateIdentity: assigned by trusted snapshotting of actual bytes; a worker-supplied digest is refused
evidencePolicy.repairDispatchNote: Counts supervisor-initiated repair dispatches after a failed protected check, not native inner test/fix iterations.

pilotObligations: Decide how this backend's containment is to be observed at all. The free battery that qualifies Codex has no equivalent here; the options are a separately authorized paid qualification dispatch, or an OS-level boundary applied from outside the SDK (which is the same work item the Codex read boundary needs).
Observe process.descendantsAfterStop. abortController stops the query; nothing establishes that descendants exited.
Obtain separate authorization before any real product dispatch (Execution Portfolio S1.4).
